title: California's 30th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 30th Congressional District pits incumbent Democrat Laura Friedman against Republican attorney Scott Meyers. The district, which includes Burbank, Glendale, West Hollywood, and parts of Los Angeles and Pasadena, is a Democratic stronghold where registered Democrats outnumber Republicans by roughly three to one. Friedman is seeking a second term after winning the seat in 2024, while Meyers advanced from a seven-candidate June 2, 2026 top-two primary as the runner-up. The outcome will help determine which party controls the U.S. House in the 119th Congress.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the general election matchup between Laura Friedman and Scott Meyers in California's 30th Congressional District as of mid-June 2026.

candidates.name: Laura Friedman
candidates.summary: Laura Friedman is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 30th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. She previously served in the California State Assembly representing the 44th district, where she chaired the Transportation and Natural Resources committees and authored legislation on road safety, zero-emission vehicles, and water conservation. Before her political career, Friedman worked as a film and television producer and served on the Glendale City Council, including a term as Mayor of Glendale.

candidates.name: Scott Meyers
candidates.summary: Scott Alan Meyers is a Republican candidate for the U.S. House in California's 30th Congressional District, having advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary as the second-place finisher. He is an attorney with 37 years of civil law experience, a small business owner, and a lifelong Southern California resident who earned his undergraduate degree from UCLA and his law degree from Pepperdine Law School. Meyers' campaign priorities include border security, election integrity, reducing federal spending, and reviving the film and television industry in California.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists for this contest, which limits confidence. However, the district is described as a Democratic stronghold where registered Democrats outnumber Republicans by roughly three to one. Incumbent Democrat Laura Friedman is seeking a second term after winning the seat in 2024, and the district has a long history of Democratic representation (previously held by Adam Schiff). Republican challenger Scott Meyers advanced from a seven-candidate top-two primary as the runner-up, but the district's fundamentals—a roughly 3:1 Democratic registration advantage combined with incumbency—point to an overwhelming Democratic advantage. In the absence of polling counter-signals, a safe Democratic rating is warranted, though confidence remains medium due to the polling gap.
